samples.summary: v1 `PATCH /documents/:did` still takes an unvalidated inline body type, so mass-assignment protection rests only on a hand-maintained allowlist
samples.evidence: `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }` (documents.controller.ts:115) is a TypeScript inline type, not a DTO class. The global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })` (main.ts:66-71) skips validation entirely when the parameter metatype is `Object`, so *nothing* filters this body — the change's own spec acknowledges this (documents.controller.spec.ts: "the body is an inline type, not a DTO class, so the global ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }) strips nothing here"). The handler is currently safe only because it copies `title` and `folderId` across one field at a time; the previous version spread the whole body into `prisma.document.update` (the vulnerability this diff removes), and a single future edit reintroducing a spread re-opens writing `workspaceId`, `authorID`, `fileId`, `type` from the request. Secondary effect today: `title` has no type/length check and `folderId` has no `@IsUUID`, so a JSON value such as `{"folderId": {"not": "x"}}` or a non-UUID string reaches `folderService.assertSameWorkspace` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({ where: { id: <value> } })` and surfaces as an unhandled Prisma error (500) rather than a 400. The sibling web route already uses a validated `UpdateDocumentDto` (document.controller.ts:314) and the new folders controller uses `UpdateFolderDto`; this route is the odd one out. Fix: give it a DTO with `@IsOptional() @IsString() @Length(...)` title and `@IsOptional() @IsUUID()` folderId, so the whitelist is the enforcement rather than the developer's discipline.

samples.summary: `POST /documents/:id/copy` is newly reachable by an API key, membership-gated only, and performs unbounded server-side blob/image duplication with no per-caller quota
samples.evidence: The new route (documents.controller.ts:97-108) calls `DocumentCopyService.copy`, which for a blob document performs an S3 `CopyObject` of the source bytes (document-copy.service.ts:198-200) and for a cross-workspace copy re-hosts up to 100 images / 64 MB (MAX_REHOSTED_IMAGES, MAX_REHOSTED_BYTES). The v1 gate is workspace membership only — deliberately not the manager bar — so any holder of a write-scoped key (or any member) can loop `copy` against the largest blob document in the workspace. `ApiV1FoldersController` and `ApiV1DocumentsController` carry no `@Throttle` override, so only the global 120 req/60 s bucket applies, and there is no storage quota per workspace or per key: ~120 copies/min of a max-size upload is gigabytes/minute of attacker-chosen storage growth from a single credential. The web equivalent (`POST documents/:id/copy`, document.controller.ts:296) has the same shape under a session, so this is exposure of an existing design to an unattended, scriptable credential rather than a new class of bug — hence low confidence that it is treated as a defect here. Worth a per-key or per-workspace quota, or at least a tighter `@Throttle` on the copy route as `images`/`files` already do.

samples.summary: Folder delete cascades to descendant folders authored by other members, so a folder author can destroy another member's subtree — now scriptable via an API key
samples.evidence: `remove` gates on `isManager` = workspace owner OR `folder.authorID === userId` (folders.controller.ts:76-86, 147-155), then calls `folderService.delete(folderId)` → `prisma.folder.delete`. In schema.prisma:137 the self-relation is `parent Folder? @relation("FolderTree", ..., onDelete: Cascade)`, so every descendant folder is deleted with it regardless of who authored it. Member B, who created a sub-folder under member A's folder, has their folder destroyed when A deletes theirs; A is not a manager of B's folder. The comment at folders.controller.ts:153-154 ("Non-destructive by schema") is accurate only about documents (`Document.folder` is `onDelete: SetNull`, schema.prisma:123), not about the folder structure itself. Behaviour is identical to the JWT web route (folder.controller.ts:106-119), so this is pre-existing rather than introduced — but the new surface makes it reachable by an unattended credential, and the reasoning comment slightly overstates the safety. No document data loss, hence nit.
